text: Before you create a single legal entity or ledger, you need the map. Oracle Fusion's enterprise structures are a handful of interlocking blocks, and this lesson is that map.

A legal entity is a real, registered organization — the legal "who." A ledger is the accounting book that records a legal entity's transactions, using one chart of accounts, one calendar, one currency. A business unit processes transactions. The chart of accounts classifies everything.

These pieces are assigned to each other in a layered way. Legal entities are assigned to a ledger. That ledger uses one chart of accounts and one calendar. Business units are assigned to a ledger, and usually a legal entity. Get an assignment wrong, and transactions post to the wrong books.

Every later course in this path assumes these four structures already exist and are assigned correctly. You can't post an invoice without a business unit, run a business unit without a ledger, or have a ledger without a chart of accounts.

Legal entities, ledgers, business units, and the chart of accounts — four blocks, explicitly assigned to one another. Next up, lesson four: Functional Setup Manager, the tool that generates the task lists you'll use to build these structures.
